text:
You want me white,

you want me made of foam,

you want me of mother-of-pearl.

That I be a lily,

chaste above all others,

of faint perfume.

A closed corolla.


Not a ray of moonlight

may have filtered through me.

May no daisy

call itself my sister.

You want me snowy,

you want me white,

you want me dawn-white.


You who had every

cup within reach,

your lips purple

with fruits and honey.

You who at the banquet

covered in vine leaves

left your flesh

celebrating Bacchus.

You who in the gardens

black with Deceit,

dressed in red,

ran toward Ruin.


You who still keep

your skeleton intact

by miracles

I cannot fathom,

you demand me white

(God forgive you),

you demand me chaste

(God forgive you),

you demand me dawn-white!


Flee toward the woods,

go to the mountain;

cleanse your mouth;

live in huts;

touch with your hands

the wet earth;

feed your body

on bitter root;

drink from the rocks;

sleep upon frost;

renew your tissues

with saltpeter and water:


Speak with the birds

and rise at dawn.

And when your flesh

has been returned to you,

and when you have placed

within it the soul

that in the bedrooms

was left tangled,

then, good man,

demand me white,

demand me snowy,

demand me chaste.

translation.title: You Want Me White
translation.editorial_note: The translation retains the poem’s accusatory repetition, Bacchic imagery, and imperative cleansing sequence. The irregular “lévate al alba” is rendered as “rise at dawn.”
